French government admits it was unprepared for the level of chaos unleashed by rioters, which forced civilians to protect their businesses
3 -MIN READ 3 -MIN 4 Listen Xiaofei Xu in Paris Published: 5:00pm, 20 Oct 2026 Updated: 5:14pm, 20 Oct 2026 Two days have passed since the scenes of chaos and looting on Saturday , but walking down Rue Beaurepaire in Paris on Monday, one can still smell smoke in the air, likely coming from the heaps of burned rubbish and charred bicycles left among the smashed shopfronts. Among the most damaged was La Barrique, a local bar-tabac – a French establishment combining a cafe, bar and tobacco shop – that was burned down by rioters . Its owner, Aline Li, a middle-aged Chinese immigrant from Zhejiang province, was overseeing workers boarding up the ruin. Her face still bore cuts and bruises from the attack on Saturday, but she also began to smile, greeting the residents who came by to check in on her.
“I’m fine, what matters is that you guys are also OK,” she said.
